questions.subject: WORLD_HISTORY
questions.learningObjective: explain why the Crimea pledge on free elections could not be enforced
questions.stem: At the Crimea conference in February 1945 the three great powers promised free and unfettered elections in liberated Europe, but set no date, no method of counting, and no outside observer. Which statement best explains why that omission mattered more than the promise itself?

options.text: The text bound the powers to consult one another, not to guarantee an outcome, so a state that staged a vote could claim the pledge had been honoured
The omission meant every liberated state was held by Soviet troops, which no wording could ever have prevented
options.misconception: reads an absence of enforcement machinery as a statement about the physical position of armies

options.text: The pledge was legally void because two of the three powers never signed the conference protocol
options.misconception: invents a missing signature that the record of the conference contradicts

options.text: The omission allowed a liberated state to decline elections entirely without contradicting the text
options.misconception: treats silence about dates as permission to avoid elections rather than as permission to delay them

questions.explanation: The declaration asked the three powers to consult together and to support interim governments broadly representative of democratic elements, but fixed no deadline, franchise rule, or verification. A promise with no checking mechanism can be read as satisfied by the very actor it was meant to restrain, which is why two sides could each claim the other had broken a text they had both signed. The wrong answers either describe a military fact the wording never addressed, invent a defect in the signatures, or turn silence about timing into an exemption from voting.
questions.hint: Ask what a promise without any checking procedure can actually compel a government to do.

questions.subject: WORLD_HISTORY
questions.learningObjective: trace the consequences of a provisional border arranged without a treaty
questions.stem: At Potsdam in the summer of 1945 the three powers agreed that German territory east of the Oder and western Neisse rivers should be placed under Polish administration pending a final settlement, while fixing no frontier in a treaty. Which consequence followed most directly from that arrangement?

options.text: The three powers split the territory into three of their own occupation zones until a plebiscite chose the owner
options.misconception: reads an administrative decision as a temporary division awaiting a popular vote

options.text: Poland governed and settled the territory at once, and the absence of a treaty left the permanent frontier to be settled later by the fact of administration
The territory returned to Germany because no peace treaty was ever signed confirming the change
options.misconception: treats an unratified arrangement as automatically void rather than as an unsettled position on the ground

options.text: Poland refused the administration because the final settlement had not been agreed in advance
options.misconception: supposes a state would decline offered territory in order to avoid an unresolved legal status

questions.explanation: The conference gave Poland the administration of the territory without giving it the title, and the settlers, officials, and police went in immediately. A frontier that is administered for years without a treaty is fixed in practice long before it is fixed in law, which is why the later dispute was about whether to recognise a fact rather than about how to apply an agreement. The other answers convert an administrative decision into a plebiscite, a nullity, or a refusal.
questions.hint: Ask who actually lived in and ran the territory during the years while the final settlement was postponed.

questions.subject: WORLD_HISTORY
questions.learningObjective: assess the occupation settlement as an arrangement for control rather than for government
questions.stem: The three great powers, with France added, divided Germany into occupation zones whose boundaries cut across industrial regions and a single railway network, and put Berlin under joint administration although the city lay deep inside the Soviet zone. Which statement about that design is soundest?

options.text: Berlin was assigned to joint administration because its factories had suffered less damage than any other German city in the war
options.misconception: explains a political decision by the relative survival of industrial plant

options.text: The zones were drawn to follow pre-war provincial boundaries so that administration could continue undisturbed from 1939 onward
options.misconception: assumes the boundaries were chosen to preserve existing administrative units

options.text: It was an arrangement for controlling a defeated state rather than a plan for running one economy, so it produced a standing bargaining problem instead of a working state
The zones were intended as the permanent states that a peace conference would ratify within a few months
options.misconception: converts a provisional occupation into a completed partition intended to last

questions.explanation: The zones were drawn to allocate control among the victors, so they paid no attention to the coal, the steel, or the railways that made a modern economy one unit. The result was a state whose economy could only function as a whole being administered as four parts, and a decision in one part immediately became a problem for the other three. The distractors either treat the boundaries as chosen for administrative continuity, explain the capital's status by war damage, or describe the settlement as a finished partition rather than a provisional one.
questions.hint: Ask whether the boundaries were chosen to match the factories and the railways or to divide the spoils of victory.

questions.subject: WORLD_HISTORY
questions.learningObjective: read a summary of the Potsdam terms for the aims it names and the trade it implies

stimulus.body: A modern summary of the Potsdam protocol records that the occupying powers resolved to disarm and disband the German armed forces, to destroy the National Socialist party and its affiliated organisations, to decentralise the German economy and prepare for the reconstruction of democratic political life, and to take reparations chiefly from each power's own zone, with an additional share for the Soviet Union drawn from the western zones in exchange for food, coal, and raw materials.
stimulus.license: original text written for this bank; no protected source reproduced

questions.stem: Read the summary. Which statement about what that protocol establishes is soundest?

options.text: It barred France from the occupation because France had not been present at the earlier great-power conference
options.misconception: supposes an exclusion of a power that received a zone of its own

options.text: It created a single German state with a federal constitution and a central bank to govern it
options.misconception: reads a list of occupation aims as the founding text of a new constitution

options.text: It fixed the date on which all occupying forces would withdraw from Germany
options.misconception: invents a withdrawal timetable that the summary does not contain

options.text: It named four allied aims and made a Soviet claim on western industrial output depend on a Soviet supply of goods

questions.explanation: The summary gives four political aims in plain terms and then makes reparations zonal in principle with a western draw for the Soviet Union, so the Soviet share of western output was tied to deliveries in the other direction. That trade is the checkable feature of the settlement, and it is what made the whole arrangement vulnerable: a withdrawal of food, or a refusal to deliver equipment, unravelled a clause on which the rest depended. The other answers report a constitution, a withdrawal date, and a French exclusion, none of which the text or the record supports.
questions.hint: Look for the clause that makes one side's claim depend on the other side's deliveries.

questions.subject: WORLD_HISTORY
questions.learningObjective: infer the economic consequences of a zonal reparations settlement
questions.stem: A study gives the share of German industrial capacity available for reparations in each zone under the Potsdam settlement: about one quarter in the Soviet zone, about one third each in the British and American zones, with an additional share for the Soviet Union drawn from the western zones in exchange for food and raw materials. Which conclusion does the table best support?

options.text: The settlement guaranteed that the Soviet Union received the largest single share of industrial capacity of any power
options.misconception: reads a supplementary claim on western output as a larger share of the total than the zones themselves held

options.text: Soviet recovery was linked to western production, so the settlement made the western powers' own zones harder to run the more they paid
Every power received the same reparations figure regardless of what industry its own zone contained
options.misconception: assumes equal shares in a settlement that divided the country into zones of unequal weight

options.text: The settlement transferred whole factories from the western zones into the Soviet zone as its main mechanism
options.misconception: confuses current production taken as reparations with the physical removal of plant

questions.explanation: Because reparations were to come chiefly from each power's own zone, the Soviet Union could take most from the smallest industrial zone, and its access to western output was arranged as an addition paid for in food and materials. That created a chain in which Soviet recovery depended on western production, and western recovery depended on not paying out too much, so each side had a reason to put its own zone first. The distractors either rank the shares incorrectly, assume equality, or describe removals of equipment rather than deliveries of output.
questions.hint: Ask whose output the extra Soviet share had to come from, and who then paid for it.

questions.subject: WORLD_HISTORY
questions.learningObjective: analyse why two allied aims for the same state could not both be satisfied
questions.stem: After 1945 each state between Germany and the Soviet Union had western sponsors who wanted elections and a Soviet sponsor who wanted a friendly government in place. Which statement best explains why the two aims could not both be satisfied in the same state?

options.text: Both sides preferred appointed governments, but each wanted the appointments made in a different capital
options.misconception: claims a shared preference for appointment that the western position contradicts

options.text: The two sides disagreed only about the dates on which elections should be held, not about their outcome
options.misconception: reduces a conflict over principles of legitimacy to a calendar dispute

options.text: Each side was applying a different test to the same election, so a vote that looked free to one side looked insecure to the other
The two sides agreed on elections and disagreed only about which single party should be permitted to stand
options.misconception: locates the disagreement in the party lists rather than in what a lawful result was

questions.explanation: The western test was whether the ballot was free and unfettered; the Soviet test was whether the resulting government would be one the Soviet Union could live with. A genuinely open vote in a state with a strong communist party and a strong democratic opposition could pass the first test and fail the second, which is why the same event could be called a triumph by one power and a threat by the other. Treating the dispute as being about dates, about a shared preference for appointment, or about the list of candidates misses that the parties were measuring different things.
questions.hint: Ask which question each side was really asking when it looked at the ballot.

questions.subject: WORLD_HISTORY
questions.learningObjective: explain how the 1945 settlements left the fate of eastern Europe open
questions.stem: Explain why the agreements made in 1945 about liberated Europe failed to remove the competition between the great powers over the states lying between Germany and the Soviet Union.

answer.exemplar: The 1945 settlements recorded four things and left a fifth out. They recorded a promise of free elections, an agreement about where the armies stood, an agreement about how reparations would be taken, and an agreement about the aims of the occupation of Germany. What they did not record was any mechanism by which a third party could decide whether the first promise had been kept. The effect was that each great power could claim to be honouring the agreement while charging the other with breaking it, because neither had accepted a test it could be held to. A promise of consultation with no procedure for consultation is a statement of intent, and a settlement that names the aims of an occupation without naming the government that will carry them out leaves the decisive question to the armies already on the ground. Competition therefore continued, and it continued inside a text that both sides had signed and could quote against each other.

questions.explanation: The answer works because it separates what the settlement fixed, the positions of the armies and the rules for reparations, from what it left undefined, the way to test a promise of free elections. Because no verification mechanism existed, the same clause could be invoked by both sides and enforced by neither, so the field was left to the power already present. Naming that gap, rather than blaming one side, is what explains the outcome.
questions.hint: Ask which of the settlement's clauses could be tested by anyone, and which could only be asserted.

questions.subject: WORLD_HISTORY
questions.learningObjective: synthesise the relative value of the elections clause and the zonal settlement
questions.stem: A negotiator at the Crimea conference insisted that the clause on liberated Europe was the whole point of the meeting, while a colleague on the same delegation argued that an unverifiable promise was worth less than the concrete agreement on occupation zones. Which statement best describes the two positions together?

options.text: Neither position matters, since the conference set no policy at all concerning eastern Europe
options.misconception: overstates by treating an unenforced pledge as identical to no pledge at all

options.text: The negotiator must be wrong, since the clause on liberated Europe never appeared in the final text of the agreement
options.misconception: denies the existence of a clause that was in fact published as part of the declaration

options.text: The colleague must be wrong, since the occupation zones were redrawn entirely after the conference broke up
options.misconception: claims the zonal map was revised in ways the record does not support

options.text: Both were right, because the clause fixed what the west could demand in future while the zones fixed what each side already held, and each side paid in a different currency

questions.explanation: The clause on liberated Europe and the agreement on zones did different work. The zones recorded an existing military fact and gave each power something it could defend without anyone's permission, while the elections clause created a standing standard by which later conduct could be judged. Each side therefore gained something real, and each gained something that could not be converted into the other's currency, which is why the bargain held at the time and the dispute continued for years afterwards. The wrong answers dismiss one position by denying a clause that exists, or by denying a revision that never happened.
questions.hint: Ask which part of the agreement described what already existed and which part described what ought to happen.

questions.subject: WORLD_HISTORY
questions.learningObjective: explain how zonal control of the coercive ministries decided political outcomes
questions.stem: After 1945 the ministries of the interior, defence, and justice in each state between Germany and the Soviet Union passed into the hands of one party in each government, while the other ministries remained in other hands. Which statement about that pattern is soundest?

options.text: The pattern was accidental, since the portfolios were distributed by cabinet rotation rather than by design
options.misconception: attributes to chance a distribution that was contested at every stage

options.text: Control of police, courts, and appointment turned a constitutional coalition into a one-party state without any amendment to the law
The pattern mattered little, since each ministry operated independently under the terms of the constitution
options.misconception: treats ministries as independent when the coercive ones decide who may act

options.text: The pattern was reversed after 1948, when the opposition was given the interior ministry in every state
options.misconception: asserts a transfer of coercive power that never took place

questions.explanation: A ministry of the interior decides which parties may meet, which newspapers may print, and which officials are appointed; a ministry of justice decides which of those decisions is lawful. When the party that held those portfolios was the same party that wanted to exclude its rivals, the constitutional guarantee of opposition was satisfied in form while being emptied in substance, because the guarantees were administered by the offices that opposed them. The coalition survived on paper until the merger of the parties removed the last ministers of the other side. The wrong answers treat the pattern as chance, as harmless, or as reversed.
questions.hint: Ask which ministries decide whether an opposition party may legally exist and publish.

questions.subject: WORLD_HISTORY
questions.learningObjective: read an observer's account for what it establishes about the conditions of a ballot

stimulus.body: An original record of an observer appointed by a western diplomatic mission to a Polish district for the election of January 1947: 'In this district the lists of the opposition party were rejected by the local board on the ground that two of its candidates had served as officers in an organisation under the occupation. In the villages the voters were handed one ballot for the state list and were asked to mark it in full view of the presiding officer. The police were seated at the tables and recorded the numbers of the envelopes. In three villages no other ballot was distributed at all. The returning officer told me that the result of this district had been reported to the ministry before the count was finished.'
stimulus.license: original text written for this bank; no protected source reproduced

questions.stem: Read the record. Which statement about what the observer found is best supported?

options.text: The observer recorded that the opposition won the district but the ministry refused to accept the count
options.misconception: invents a contested victory that the record does not describe

options.text: The observer certified that the vote had been conducted properly apart from a handful of errors in a single district
options.misconception: converts a report of systematic defects into a general certificate of fairness

options.text: The conditions of the ballot and the count were controlled by one side before any vote was recorded, so the result measures administration rather than preference
The observer recorded that voters marked ballots in private and that his own tallies agree with the announced result
options.misconception: asserts secrecy and agreement that the record explicitly contradicts

questions.explanation: Each detail in the record removes one of the conditions of a free ballot: the opposition was struck off in advance, the voter marked one ballot in the open, the police recorded the envelopes, and in three villages no alternative existed at all. When the returning officer also describes the result being reported to the ministry before the count finished, the observer is describing a procedure whose outcome was settled before polling rather than a verdict of the voters. The wrong answers turn a report of systematic control into a certificate, a disputed win, or a confirmation of secrecy.
questions.hint: Ask which of the ordinary conditions of a ballot the record shows was missing.
